newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends near daily high on run cut talks.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends near daily high on run cut talks.

text.p: IPE June gas oil closed $2.75 a tonne higher at $179.00 on Thursday and traders said the rally was partly fuelled by fears that European and Asian refiners would cut their runs due to worsening margins.
June gas oil hit a high of $179.50 during the day but also sank earlier to trader as low as $177.25. July gas oil also closed higher at $179.50 or $2.00 a tonne up on Wednesday's close.

"The market was generally quiet today and continues to be dominated by spreads which are continuing to narrow. I don't think it (rise) is necessarily on the way the market has been treating demand, demand is very sluggish at the moment," one trader said.
"I think the rally is mainly that people are concerned that refineries may cut their runs in Europe and many, many parts of Asia. Then people would have to look for substitutes," the trader added.
Traders said on Thursday afternoon that British Petroleum cut refinery runs at its Rotterdam refinery by 40 percent from midnight on Wednesday due to poor margins.

They said BP, which controls 65 percent of 400,000 bpd Rotterdam Nerefco refinery, had cut runs by the equivalent of 10 percent for the month of May, which translated into a 40 percent cut for the balance of May.
Last week, Texaco cut crude runs at the refinery by the equivalent of 20 percent for the second half of May.
But other ARA refiners were holding back from cutting runs on Thursday, traders said.
The recent rise in Brent crude prices since the start of the month by about $2.50 has caused refiners margins in Europe and the Middle East to suffer.

IPE July Brent was trading at roughly its afternoon levels when the contract hit a high of $20.34 after NYMEX opened then moved to the $20.28 area. By 1704 GMT, July Brent was trading 14 cents a barrel up at $20.27.
